Gun position before the target appears

At a Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ competition, shooters call for the target with the gun held low. This is a rule, not a matter of style. Compak® Sporting has no such rule.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Gun low: the top back of the stock is kept under the vest line until you see the target.

Compak® Sporting

Free: the gun may already be at the shoulder, or lower. There is no line on the vest, but the shot is still fired from the shoulder.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

In Sporting™, before you call, both your feet are inside the stand. The heel of the stock (its top back corner, the part that goes into your shoulder) touches your body. The highest back point of the stock, usually the heel itself, stays below the line on the vest. You keep this ready position until the target has left the trap and you can see it.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 3 · Ready position: feet and gun

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

The line is marked on the vest or jacket 25 cm below the shoulder axis (an imaginary horizontal line through both shoulders), parallel to it. Its colour stands out against the vest, so the referee can see it. The rule covers all kinds of stock: standard, Monte Carlo (with a raised comb, the top edge of the stock where your cheek rests) and adjustable comb.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 3 · The 25 cm marking line on the jacket

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

You may bring the gun up to your shoulder (mount it) only once the target appears. All targets, the rabbit too, are shot with the gun at the shoulder; shooting from the hip is not allowed.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 3 · When the gun may be mounted

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

One relaxation: in a double, you may hold the gun as you like between the first and the second target. Before the first target the low position still applies.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 3 · Gun position between the two targets of a double

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Penalties: the first time you call in a wrong position or mount the gun too early, the referee gives a spoken warning and shows a yellow card. Doing it again on the same layout costs a red card: a single is scored zero, and doubles follow the table in the rules guide (Chapter 12 · Red card on repeat at the same layout).

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 12 · Yellow card for gun position

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Mounting the gun and swinging it along the line where you expect the target, before you call, is mock shooting, and it is forbidden too. The first time brings a warning. If it happens again, the next target you hit is scored zero.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 8 · Mock shooting and accidental shots

Tip: If you shoot both disciplines, many coaches suggest training the low-gun start before a Sporting™ event, even if you call gun-up in Compak® Sporting.

Key points

  • Sporting™: before the call, both feet in the stand, the heel of the stock (its top back corner) on your body and below the vest line.
  • Sporting™: the vest line is 25 cm below the shoulder axis (a line through both shoulders), in a contrasting colour.
  • Sporting™: mount only when the target appears; the gun position is free only between the two targets of a double.
  • Sporting™: the first offence brings a warning with a yellow card, the next one on the same layout a red card.
  • Compak® Sporting: the position at the call is free and there is no vest line; the shot is still fired from the shoulder.

Did you know?

The low-gun start is often explained by the hunting roots of Sporting™: a hunter rarely waits for a bird with the gun already at the shoulder.

Stand Talk

  • Referee Gun down, please.

    Meaning: Referee: bring the stock below the vest line before calling.

  • Referee Your stock was above the line. This is a warning.

    Meaning: First gun-position offence: verbal warning with a yellow card.

  • Referee Don't mount before the target appears.

    Meaning: The gun may come up only once the target is visible.

  • Referee Red card, zero.

    Meaning: A repeat offence on the same layout; the single is lost.

  • Coach Butt under the tape until you see the target.

    Meaning: Sporting™ gun-down rule: the stock stays below the vest line until the target appears.

  • Coach No marker needed here — it's Compak.

    Meaning: Compak® Sporting has no vest-line requirement.

  • Coach Gun up or down, your choice here.

    Meaning: Coach: in Compak® Sporting the gun position at the call is free.

For the interpreter
  • If a coach drills a gun-up start before a Sporting™ event, make sure the word 'drill' is translated too: it is an exercise, not the competition start.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. How far below the shoulder axis (an imaginary line through both shoulders) is the vest line in Sporting™?

    1. 10 cm
    2. 25 cm
    3. 40 cm
    Answer

    25 cm

    The line runs 25 cm below the shoulder axis, parallel to it.

    Chapter 3 · The 25 cm marking line on the jacket

  2. May you call for the target in Compak® Sporting with the gun already at the shoulder?

    1. No, the gun must start low
    2. Only when shooting a double
    3. Yes, the position is free
    Answer

    Yes, the position is free

    Compak® Sporting has no low-gun rule and no vest line; only the shot itself must be fired from the shoulder.

    Chapter 17 · Gun position when calling

  3. When may you hold the gun as you like in Sporting™?

    1. Between the two targets of a double
    2. Before the first target of a double
    3. While waiting for a rabbit
    Answer

    Between the two targets of a double

    The free position is allowed only between the two targets of a double; before the first one the ready position applies.

    Chapter 3 · Gun position between the two targets of a double
